title: Kyle's character: a Vigilant of Stendarr
description: Kyle’s own character for our Skyrim Together campaign: a Breton Vigilant of Stendarr from Cyrodiil. Character card, lore, quotes, how to play him, the nearest shrine to Helgen, and story hooks.
lead: This is Kyle's own character. Everyone else plays their own.
He is a Breton man from Cyrodiil and a Vigilant of Stendarr. He walks north to find his order.
Each fact below says where it came from. What we have not checked says so.
UESP is a fan-run game wiki. The clip is a fan video, and it is labelled wherever we use it.

grids.title: At a glance
rows: Who is he?
A Breton man. A Vigilant of Stendarr, from Cyrodiil.
Where do we meet him?
On the road north into Skyrim, near Helgen. He is not escaping Helgen's execution.
What does he want?
To reach his order, or get back to it. A Stendarr shrine can be his base.
How far will he fall?
Open. Play decides it.
Will he join the Dawnguard?
Open. Play decides it.
Does the party start together?
Maybe not. It may start scattered. A couple of us may meet in a town.
How does he play?
Healer first. He keeps the party alive before he attacks.

items.title: His vow
items.text: He vows to pass gold and spare gear to his friends quickly. He gladly takes their hand-me-downs in return. It fits the fourth precept of Stendarr: do not hoard wealth or indulge.

items.title: The closest shrine
items.text: The Two Pillars, in Whiterun Hold. It is about 23 cells from Helgen in a straight line, and about 33 walking from town to town. A Stendarr shrine cures disease.

items.title: Heavy armor and his spells
items.text: Heavy armor does not weaken Restoration or Destruction in our install. Not yet tested in play. One group cares: Oakflesh, Ironflesh, Stoneflesh, Ebonyflesh and Dragonhide lose their Mage Armor bonus under any light or heavy armor.

grids.title: Lore: what the Vigil believes and does
grids.note: The clip is a fan video by one fan, not game text. Rows marked "Fan video only." are its reading.
rows: Four enemies
The Vigil hunts abominations: Daedra, werewolves, vampires and witches. The old doctrine names four kinds: Daedra, man-beasts, risen dead and vampires.
Daedra come first
Daedra and their worshippers worry the Vigil most. It treats vampires as a lesser threat. It shows no mercy to abominations.
Mercy for mortals
Four precepts. Never refuse aid you can give. Go among the sick and wounded. Pray every day. Do not hoard wealth or indulge.
Fear of dark magic
The order grew from fear after the Oblivion Crisis. It hates conjuring and necromancy. Healing and holy magic are its own. Fan video only.
On the road
Vigilants walk the roads in groups and patrol the wilds. Any Vigilant who is not fighting will cure your disease if you ask. It costs nothing.
At the hall
The Hall is a lodge and a monastery. Members eat, read and pray there. Some dig up old ruins and write notes. Fan video only.

grids.title: Traits and virtues
rows: Mercy
Stendarr is the God of Mercy. Vigilants say they bring his compassion where none can be found.
Mercy has an edge
The Vigil has no mercy for Daedra worshippers or abominations. The greeting says so.
Charity
Never refuse aid you can give. Go among the infirm and the wounded.
Daily prayer
Offer prayer to Stendarr every day.
Plain living
Do not hoard wealth or indulge. A Vigilant drops only a little gold when killed.
Healing
Every Vigilant knows Healing. Each carries two healing potions and a cure disease potion.
Study
Tolan says they always studied their enemies, to learn how to beat them.
Comradeship
The Hall was a place of respite, learning and comradeship. Vigilants walk in groups.
Endless watch
Most live as nomads, in what Tolan calls an endless war against evil.
Secrecy
The Vigil is known to use spies and agents for covert missions.
Faults, seen from outside
Isran left the Vigil. He calls them soft, and says they have more bravery than sense. That is his view, not the game’s verdict.

grids.title: How a Vigilant behaves
rows: On the road
They walk in groups and patrol the wilds. Some stand alone in set places.
First meeting
They warn you off the Daedra. See the quotes below.
You are sick
Ask, and they cure your disease for free. They want your promise never to help the Daedra.
In a fight
One-handed mace and defensive magic. All know Oakflesh, Healing and Lesser Ward. They never carry shields.
Daedra on sight
They attack Barbas in the quest A Daedra’s Best Friend. He cannot die, so they do.
A werewolf
In human form, left alone. In beast form, attacked.
A stray blow
Hit one by accident and the whole group may turn hostile. So may a Vigilant on the road you heal with Healing Hands.
Daedric gear
They ignore Daedric weapons, armor and conjured Atronachs near them, despite their words. A scene where they demand Daedric artifacts is in the game data, switched off.
After the Hall falls
They keep acting as if the Hall stands and Carcette lives.

items.title: Do not heal a Vigilant on the road
items.text: UESP says a Vigilant healed with Healing Hands out on the road may turn hostile. Striking one by accident can turn them all hostile. Heal your party, not their patrols.

grids.title: What they hunt, and why
rows: Daedra

The worst of them. Profane creatures with no hope of redemption. They lure innocents to death and corrupt the souls they touch. Their artifacts give mortals power, so the artifacts must be destroyed or guarded.
Daedra worshippers
The Vigil’s main concern. A Vigil journal says it will torture them for information.
Vampires
Hated, but ranked below Daedra. Curing vampirism was seen as blasphemy. After the Hall burns, Tolan says vampires are worse than Daedra.
Werewolves
Named among the abominations. Some Vigilants fight beside the Silver Hand, the werewolf hunters.
Witches
Named among the abominations. UESP gives no example in Skyrim.
The Mythic Dawn
In 4E 201 the Vigil chased this cult in Skyrim. It is the cult behind the Oblivion Crisis.
Who they leave alone
No action against Orc strongholds that worship Malacath. UESP says it is unknown if they oppose Azura or Meridia.

grids.title: The temples, the Dawnguard and the Thalmor
rows: The Temple of Stendarr
Vigilants are part of the Priesthood of Stendarr. Each province has a chapter led by a Keeper of the Vigil.
Priests of other Divines
Florentius Baenius, a priest of Arkay, worked with the Vigil. They sent him to Ruunvald, and he was captured.
Shrines
Shrines of Stendarr stand across Skyrim, from the wilds to the Temple of the Divines in Solitude. The Hall and Stendarr’s Beacon each hold one.
The Dawnguard
Close ties. Two former Vigilants, Isran and Celann, restarted it. Isran thought the Vigil too soft. When vampires burned the Hall, Tolan went to Isran for help.
The Silver Hand
Some Vigil members have ties to the Silver Hand, with dog motifs on their armor.
The Thalmor
UESP names no link between the Vigil and the Thalmor in Skyrim. Open. Anything here is our own story.
Elves and Stendarr
Stendarr sits in the Altmer pantheon too. A minority of elves frown on worshipping him, as the Apologist of Men.

grids.title: Lore: what a Vigilant must know
grids.note: Yes, the clip names alchemy, restoration and destruction. The clip is a fan video. It says Vigilants must learn all three and fight with maces. It gives no game source for must.
rows: Alchemy
Must learn it. The Hall has two alchemy labs.
Each Vigilant carries healing potions and a cure disease potion.
Restoration
Must learn it. Healing is their trade.
Every Vigilant knows the Healing spell.
Destruction
Must learn it. The fan video says they add fire magic to the mace.
The list shows no fire spell for a Skyrim Vigilant. Fan video only.
Mace
Vigilants fight with maces.
Each Vigilant carries a mace. It gets better as they level.
Defense
They cast a protective armor spell before a fight.
Every Vigilant knows Oakflesh and Lesser Ward.
Jack of all trades
They know a little of everything. Few master any of it. Fan video only.
Not stated.

grids.title: Lore: history
rows: Founding
The Vigil was founded soon after the Oblivion Crisis of 3E 433. Older Stendarr orders came before it.
In Skyrim
The Hall of the Vigilant is south of Dawnstar. A second base, Stendarr's Beacon, is a tower in The Rift. Keeper Carcette leads.
Isran and Celann
Both left the Vigil, unhappy with it. Isran thought it too soft. They founded the Dawnguard.
The Hall falls
In the Dawnguard story, vampires destroy the Hall. Tolan and Adalvald die at Dimhollow Crypt. Tolan tells Isran that Carcette is dead.
After
The Vigil goes on. Most members already live on the road. Stendarr's Beacon is still a base.

items.title: “Walk always in the light, or we will drag you to it.”
items.text: Found. It is a Vigilant’s road greeting in Skyrim, one of six. The fan video quotes it too, while it talks about the spell Stendarr’s Aura (at 15:48).

grids.title: Quotes: what Vigilants say in the game
grids.note: Word for word from UESP’s dialogue lists, checked against the saved pages. Lines marked Dawnguard are from that add-on.
rows: “Walk always in the light, or we will drag you to it.”
One of six greetings on the road.
“You speak to a Vigilant of Stendarr. Cavort with any Daedra, and we will hunt you down.”
The first time you meet a Vigilant.
“Stendarr’s Mercy be upon you, for the Vigil has none to spare.”
Another road greeting.
“Wherever the Daedra hide, the Vigil of Stendarr will cast them into the light.”
Another road greeting.
“Well met, friend. We’ve been chasing that fiend for a long time. On behalf of the Vigil, you have my thanks.”
After you help a group fight an abomination.
“None escape the Vigil. All come into the light.”
A goodbye.
“The Vigil will be watching you.”
A goodbye.
“Stendarr’s Light purify you of your ills.”
When they cure your disease.
“He is the God of Mercy. The patron of order and justice for all of Tamriel. We bring his compassion where none can be found, by cleansing all those who would offend his children.”
Asking “Who’s Stendarr?”
“And any other abominations that prey on mortals. Vampires. Werewolves. Witches. But the Daedra are the worst.”
Asking “You hunt daedra?”
“The Hall was a place of respite, learning and comradeship, where a road-weary brother or sister could rest for a time in peace and comfort.”
Vigilant Tolan, Dawnguard. Asking about the Hall.
“Most of us spend our lives as nomads, traveling from place to place in our endless war against evil.”
Vigilant Tolan, Dawnguard.
“The Vigilants always had more bravery than sense.”
Isran, who left the Vigil. Dawnguard.

grids.title: Quotes: from Stendarr books
grids.note: Precepts, Four Abominations and The Sounding Horn are lore books from The Elder Scrolls Online. They are not in Skyrim. Notes on Dimhollow Crypt and Discovering Ruunvald are Skyrim books from the Dawnguard add-on.
rows: “Never refuse aid you are capable of providing.”
Precepts of Stendarr, by Ptolus the Bright, a Resolute of Stendarr. First precept.
“Go among the infirm and the wounded wherever you find them.”
Precepts of Stendarr. Second precept.
“Offer prayer to Stendarr every day.”
Precepts of Stendarr. Third precept.
“Do not hoard wealth or indulge physically.”
Precepts of Stendarr. Fourth precept.
“Be kind and generous to the people of Tamriel. Protect the weak, heal the sick, and give to the needy.”
Precepts of Stendarr. Its closing command.
“Know these Four Abominations, O ye righteous, and gather to slay them where’re they appear.”
The Four Abominations, by Vinicius Imbrex, Archbishop of Chorrol.
“Threefold are the masteries of Stendarr. I sound the horn in his name. May his shield protect me always from harm.”
The Sounding Horn. A prayer to say.
“I must return to the Hall of the Vigilant and share these findings with my brothers and sisters.”
Notes on Dimhollow Crypt, Vol. 3, by the Vigilant Adalvald.

rows.text: UESP: Notes on Dimhollow Crypt, Vol. 3

rows: “For now, Dimhollow Crypt might be a mystery, but by Stendarr I will see that mystery solved.”
Notes on Dimhollow Crypt, Vol. 3.

rows.text: UESP: Notes on Dimhollow Crypt, Vol. 3

rows: “I am certain that there is some artifact of great power to be found in those ruins, one that the Vigilants could find useful in their mission.”
Discovering Ruunvald, Vol. I, by Moric Sidrey.

grids.title: Playing him: a Breton
grids.note: The first three rows are the base game. Our server changes races. Read the fourth row.
rows: Skill bonuses
+10 Conjuration. +5 Alchemy, Alteration, Illusion, Restoration and Speech. Restoration and Alchemy are his trade.
Resist magic
25% magic resistance, always on.
Racial power
Dragonskin: absorb 50% of the magicka from hostile spells for 60 seconds, once a day.
On our server
Our server runs Imperious. It gives Bretons a power called
. Conditional on the rules page. We have not checked every other Breton change.
Bretons he may meet
Keeper Carcette leads the Vigil. Celann is a former Vigilant at Fort Dawnguard.

grids.title: Playing him: the build
rows: Armor
Heavy. Maybe some light.
See the armor grid below.
Weapon
Mace, shield, or both.
Skyrim Vigilants carry a mace.
Main skill
Restoration.
Heal others first. Keep the party standing.
Other skills
Alchemy and Destruction.
The Vigil's other disciplines, from the fan video.
Spells to try
All are Allowed on the rules page. Healing other players in co-op is not fully tested.

paragraphs: Co-op note. Potions he brews and gear he enchants may not pass between players under Skyrim Together. Reports say a crafted potion or enchanted item can fail to reach another player. We have not tested it in our pack. Wednesday’s test checks it. Until then, brew for yourself first.

grids.title: Heavy armor and spells
grids.note: Read from the installed plugin files on 2026-10-05. Not yet tested in play. Not checked: one Imperious perk for High Elves tests armor type.
rows: Does heavy armor weaken spells?
No. We found nothing in the installed plugins that does that to Restoration or Destruction.
Does heavy armor raise spell cost?
No. The spell-cost perks do not check what armor you wear.
Is any spell tied to armor?
One group. Oakflesh, Ironflesh, Stoneflesh, Ebonyflesh and Dragonhide lose their Mage Armor bonus while you wear any light or heavy armor. The spell still works. It is the same rule as the base game.
What does heavy armor give?
More armor. Perks add 20% to 100% more rating, 25% more with three heavy pieces, and 25% more with three matching pieces. Three pieces also halve fall damage and reflect some melee hits.
What does it cost?
Perk points in the Heavy Armor tree. The Conditioning perk text says heavy armor then weighs nothing and does not slow you, so it weighs and slows without it. We have not measured that.
What does light armor give instead?
Matching light perks add armor, stamina regeneration and arrow deflection. One adds 30% spell duration with two matching elven or falmer light pieces.
Can he mix them?
The bonuses count three pieces of one kind. Keep three heavy pieces to keep the heavy bonuses. That is read from the perk text, not tested.

grids.title: Playing him: perks that fit
grids.note: Perk text is from Better Vanilla Perks as installed. Our own patch changes a few perks.
rows: Bone Breaker
Mace attacks deal 20%, 40% or 60% more damage to armor and undead.
Not listed. Ask the host.
Iron Will
Blocking is 20% to 40% more effective.
Not listed. Ask the host.
Strong Reflexes rank 1
Take 50% less power-attack damage while shield blocking.
Restoration tiers
Novice to Expert: spells of that level cost half the magicka, and you gain magicka regeneration. Respite makes healing spells restore stamina too.
Not listed. Ask the host.
Resurgence
Our patch rewrites it to 10% less magicka for Restoration spells.
Destruction tiers
Spells of each level cost half the magicka and are 20% to 50% stronger. Augmented Flames cuts fire spell cost by 20%.
Not listed. Ask the host.
Alchemist
Potions and poisons are 20% to 100% stronger. Benefactor adds 25% to good potions.
Not listed. Ask the host.

grids.title: Shrines and the road
grids.note: A cell is one square of the game map. Distances are straight lines, measured by us from the game data in our install.
rows: Whiterun Hold, on the tundra. South of Swindler's Den, northeast of Broken Fang Cave. A Zenithar shrine is in sight to the west.
Hall of the Vigilant
The Pale, on a table inside the Hall, south of Dawnstar. The shrine goes when the Dawnguard quest starts and the Hall is destroyed.
Fort Greenwall
The Rift, in the Captain's Quarter, on a dresser. North-northwest of Riften. Bandits and frostbite spiders live there.
Stendarr's Beacon
The Rift, in a tower's sleeping quarters. The Vigil still uses it, even after the Dawnguard story.
Temple of the Divines, Solitude
The big temple in Solitude, with the other Divines.

grids.title: The closest shrine to Helgen
rows: Which is closest?
The Two Pillars, in Whiterun Hold.
How far?
About 23 cells in a straight line. About 33 cells walking from town to town.
What does a shrine give?
The Blessing of Stendarr: block 10% more damage with your shield, for 8 hours. It also cures disease. That is the base game. We have not re-read it in our install.
Could the Hall be his base instead?
Yes, until the Dawnguard quest starts. Then it burns. Stendarr's Beacon is the shrine that survives, but it is far to the east.

grids.title: The road from Helgen
grids.note: UESP gives positions, not the bends of the road. We have not walked the road.
rows: Helgen
Eastern Falkreath Hold, south of Riverwood. He is on the road north, near here.
Riverwood
North, about 8 cells. It has an alchemy lab. It is south of Whiterun.
Whiterun
About 9 cells farther north.
The west road
Go west from Whiterun toward Rorikstead. The shrine is about 16 cells due west of Whiterun.
Swindler's Den
East of Rorikstead. Bandits live there. The shrine is south of it.
The Two Pillars
A raised stone platform with the shrine between two standing pillars. A strong box sits beside it.
Broken Fang Cave
Southwest of the shrine. Skeletons and vampires live inside. Minimum level 6.

grids.title: People he might meet
rows: Keeper Carcette
Leads the Vigil in Skyrim, from the Hall. In the Dawnguard story Tolan says she is dead.
Isran
A Redguard and a former Vigilant. He leads the Dawnguard at Fort Dawnguard. He trains Heavy Armor.
Celann
A Breton and a former Vigilant. A vampire hunter at Fort Dawnguard.
Florentius Baenius
An Imperial priest who believes Arkay speaks through him. He worked with the Vigil and is rescued at Ruunvald. He trains Restoration.

grids.title: Story hooks
rows: A pair on the road
Vigilants walk in groups. He meets two and asks after the Hall.
Do they know where Carcette is?
The shrine by the cave
He prays at the Two Pillars and heals the party. Vampires wait in the cave below.
Does the party follow him in?
Before the Hall burns
The Hall stands until the Dawnguard quest starts. He races to reach it.
Does he arrive in time?
The one who left
Isran left the Vigil and called it too soft. He is looking for recruits.
Does Kyle's Vigilant join him?

text: He came north on foot from Cyrodiil, under a tan hood and winter mail. On Skyrim’s white roads he keeps his mace low and his shield ready. A wound gets his hands before an enemy gets his weapon; the Vigilant’s oath is to shelter the living. Whether the Dawnguard will one day call him remains for another road to decide.

At the table. Brings: crafting, potions brewed for friends, and Restoration healing. Keeps: the group’s quests, and a quick eye for how clues connect. Working on: hoarding. He vows to pass gold and spare gear to his friends quickly, and gladly takes their hand-me-downs in return.
